newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs slide late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs slide late.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast conventional gasoline differntials collapsed by late Tuesday as buyers disappeared ahead of a scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline.
However, New York Harbor and Midcontinent differentials showed little movement, with few players actively looking for deals.

No market reaction followed the severe storms that swept through the Houston area, players said. Two tornadoes hit Pasadena, Texas, home to several refineries, though twisters did not near the facilities, according to local officials.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline futures firmed 0.45 cent to settle at 58.48 cents a gallon and July heating oil futures gained 0.51 cent to finish at 52.45 cents a gallon.
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline slipped below 4.00 cents under the July NYMEX by late in the day, down about 1.00 cent on the day.
Players attributed that weakness to the lack of demand ahead of the this evening's scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline, the main artery from the Gulf Coast to the East Coast.

No shortage of barrels was evident during the day, traders said, and no active short covering appeared. Refiners covering short positions had driven prompt differentials sharply higher several times in recent weeks as the scheduling deadlines forced players to cover commitments.
Low sulphur 55-grade jet fuel differentials jumped higher, with prompt barrels changing hands as high at 0.40 cent over the July NYMEX, up about 0.50 cent from late Monday levels, traders said.
Trading activity was very thin throughout the day, according to market players, resulting in very little movement in the differentials.
Prompt heating oil was offered at about 0.10 cent under the July NYMEX, marginally higher than the Monday level, traders said, although no confirmed deals emerged.

Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline was talked on either side of 2.65 cents under the July futures, about steady with the previous day, while offers for prompt reformulated A2 gasoline hovered near -0.25 cent under the futures.
However, prompt premium V2 gasoline was talked higher, with offers at 5.50 cents over the July NYMEX, nearly 0.50 cent up on the day.
Midcontinent products markets were unchanged to slightly weaker from Tuesday morning in very quiet activity, players said. Absolute values, however, were slightly up due to the rise in NYMEX futures.
In Group Three, prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were pegged 4.25/4.75 cents over July NYMEX and any months at 2.80/3.00 cents.
In Chicago markets, prompt unleaded was down a half cent at 3.00/3.25 cents. "With the Merc up and nothing going on it is likely to pressure down differentials," said a products trader.
